svg.title: Sentinel capability quad chart
svg.desc: One-page chart in four quadrants. Operational capability: a hub and a forward edge node joined by a measured leaf link, each serving its own console. Technical approach and discriminators: open standards at every seam, an honest risk engine, priority sync, AI that cannot compute, and an offline-verifiable supply chain. Status and milestones: what is built, partly built and open. Evidence and next steps: measured results from the generated reports, the commands that reproduce them, what fielding needs, and the demo hub's cost.
svg.text: Sentinel: conjunction assessment that works when the link does not
Capability quad chart · open-source demonstration, not fielded, accredited or endorsed · exercise and published NASA data only
Operational capability
HUB
operations center
own console, own data
EDGE
forward node
works while cut off
CDMs, urgent first
signed decisions
Leaf link, measured: CONNECTED · DEGRADED · LIMITED · DENIED
What it does
• Decide before the maneuver commit point: maneuver or not.
• Refuses a Pc the method cannot support; flags dilution.
• Cut off, each node keeps working; urgent data crosses first.
• AI routes and phrases; validated code computes; a person decides.
• Ground units see when public imagers can observe them,
and the unit's position never leaves its edge node.
For
satellite operators, space operations cells, S6/G6 staff.
Technical approach and discriminators
Approach
• CCSDS standards at every seam: CDM, OMM, OEM.
• Foster-Estes 2D Pc ported from NASA CARA, worst-case
Pc and dilution flag; named refusals, never a zero.
• NATS leaf links; priority pull, summaries first; operator
data merged without loss; decisions signed, hash-chained.
• AI tier set by measured link, marking and opt-in; any
unsupported number withheld; no code path to the maths.
• Bundle signed and verified offline before unpacking;
SBOMs; vulnerability gate with reviewed VEX; SLSA Build L2.
What alternatives often get wrong
• A Pc printed from element sets, or a refusal shown as zero.
• A low Pc read as safety, even when it is diluted.
• Last writer wins: an operator's edit silently lost.
• A hosted-only tool, or an AI that states numbers.
Status and milestones
BUILT
Risk engine, checked against 53 NASA CARA events
BUILT
Operator console, offline globe, same-origin policy
BUILT
Hub/edge sync: 6 DDIL scenarios pass on real processes
BUILT
AI decision support; routing eval of the local tier
BUILT
Pass module at the edge; OPSEC scenario 10 of 10
BUILT
Signed bundle, offline verify, SBOMs, vulnerability gate
PARTIAL
Requirement trace: 53 of 54 verified
PARTIAL
OSCAL: 9 of 37 controls implemented, 28 partial
OPEN
First signed release; CI on a hosted service
OPEN
CDM feed, operator login, leaf-link TLS, an ATO
Evidence and next steps
Measured, from the generated reports
• Pc vs NASA CARA: 53 events, worst relative error 1.5e-8
• Refusal gate: all 29 CARA-flagged events refused, 0 missed
• Thin link: urgent CDM in 12.1 s by deadline, 46.8 s FIFO
• Cut off: edge console p95 2.8 ms; no operator data lost
• OPSEC: 179 messages to the hub captured; none held the unit
Reproduce
make report
make ddil
make opsec
make airgap-selftest
make trace
Next steps to field
• Real CDM access; operator authentication (CAC/PIV)
• TLS on the leaf link; packaged hub and edge messaging
• An authorizing official, a STIG scan, an ATO
• Demo hub on AWS: about $17.50/month, no other cost
figures claimed (docs/deploy-aws.md)
Every number comes from a generated report in docs/: validation-report.md, ddil-results.md, ai-eval.md and traceability.md.
Exceptions, each with its source: the AWS cost (docs/deploy-aws.md) and the control counts (docs/compliance.md).
